    # must have a linear `linearize(x_b) -> H`
    obs_op: ObservationOperator
    prior_mean: Float[Array, " N"]
    prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator

    # x* = x_b + K(y − H x_b)
    def __call__(self, batch: Batch) -> Float[Array, " N"]: ...
    def as_analysis_step(self) -> AnalysisStep: ...


# vardax/models/threedvar.py


# today* (vardax)
class ThreeDVar(eqx.Module):
    """3D variational: minimise ‖x-x_b‖²_B + ‖y-H(x)‖²_R over x."""

    obs_op: ObservationOperator
    prior_mean: Float[Array, " N"]
    prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    minimiser: optx.AbstractMinimiser
    # today (optimistix)
    minimiser_adjoint: optx.AbstractAdjoint = optx.ImplicitAdjoint()

    # x* = argmin J(x)
    def __call__(self, batch: Batch) -> Float[Array, " N"]: ...
    def as_analysis_step(self) -> AnalysisStep: ...


# vardax/models/strong_fourdvar.py


# today* (vardax)
class StrongFourDVar(eqx.Module):
    """4DVar, strong constraint. Control = x_0."""

    forward: ForwardModel
    obs_op: ObservationOperator
    prior_mean: Float[Array, " N"]
    prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    minimiser: optx.AbstractMinimiser
    # today (optimistix)
    minimiser_adjoint: optx.AbstractAdjoint = optx.ImplicitAdjoint()
    # today (diffrax)
    forward_adjoint: dfx.AbstractAdjoint = dfx.RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint()

    # x₀* = argmin J(x₀)
    def __call__(self, batch: Batch) -> Float[Array, " N"]: ...
    def as_analysis_step(self) -> AnalysisStep: ...


# vardax/models/weak_fourdvar.py


# today* (vardax)
class WeakFourDVar(eqx.Module):
    """4DVar, weak constraint. Control = (x_0, η_1, …, η_T)."""

    forward: ForwardModel
    obs_op: ObservationOperator
    prior_mean: Float[Array, " N"]
    prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    # Q
    model_err_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    minimiser: optx.AbstractMinimiser
    # today (optimistix)

    # today (diffrax)
    forward_adjoint: dfx.AbstractAdjoint = dfx.RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint()

    # (x₀*, η*) = argmin J(x₀, η)
    def __call__(self, batch: Batch) -> Float[Array, " N"]: ...
    def as_analysis_step(self) -> AnalysisStep: ...


# vardax/models/incremental_fourdvar.py


# today* (vardax)
class IncrementalFourDVar(eqx.Module):
    """Operational 4DVar: GN outer + CG inner + CVT.

    Functionally equivalent to StrongFourDVar but with a specialised
    inner solver. Use this for production work."""

    forward: ForwardModel
    obs_op: ObservationOperator
    prior_mean: Float[Array, " N"]
    prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    config: IncrementalConfig
    # today (diffrax)
    forward_adjoint: dfx.AbstractAdjoint = dfx.RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint()

    # 𝐇_GN δx* = −∇J, repeated n_outer times
    def __call__(self, batch: Batch) -> Float[Array, " N"]: ...
    def as_analysis_step(self) -> AnalysisStep: ...


# vardax/models/fourdvarnet.py


# proposed (architecture.md); ships as FourDVarNet1D / FourDVarNet2D, built from
# sizes with solver_adjoint and no prior / grad_mod / config / forward_adjoint slots
class FourDVarNet(eqx.Module):
    """Learned 4DVar: learned prior φ_θ + learned grad modulator Φ_φ."""

    prior: Prior
    obs_op: ObservationOperator
    grad_mod: GradModulator
    config: SolverConfig
    # Adjoint through the unrolled solver:
    # today (optimistix)
    solver_adjoint: optx.AbstractAdjoint = optx.RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint()
    # Adjoint through any dynamical prior:
    # today (diffrax)
    forward_adjoint: dfx.AbstractAdjoint = dfx.RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint()

    # xₖ₊₁ = xₖ − Φ_φ(∇J, hₖ), unrolled
    def __call__(self, batch: Batch) -> Float[Array, " N"]: ...
    def as_analysis_step(self) -> AnalysisStep: ...


# vardax/models/amortized.py


# today (vardax)
class AmortizedPosterior(eqx.Module):
    """Direct q_φ(x | y) head: flow / score / regression."""

    encoder: eqx.Module
    head: eqx.Module
    config: AmortizedConfig

    # E[x | y] under q_φ
    def __call__(self, batch: Batch) -> Float[Array, " N"]: ...
    # x⁽ˢ⁾ ~ q_φ(x | y)
    def sample(
        self, batch: Batch, key: PRNGKeyArray, n: int
    ) -> Float[Array, "S N"]: ...
    # log q_φ(x | y)
    def log_prob(self, x: Float[Array, " N"], batch: Batch) -> Float[Array, ""]: ...
    def as_analysis_step(self) -> AnalysisStep: ...

records.content:
The classical DA hierarchy as first-class peer classes:

OptimalInterpolation — closed-form BLUE / OI via gaussx. Layer 0
primitive blue_analysis(x_b, y, B_op, R_op, H_op).

ThreeDVar — optimistix.GaussNewton / BFGS over the nonlinear
cost.

StrongFourDVar — control = x_0, dynamics rollout via diffrax,
adjoint via forward_adjoint slot.

WeakFourDVar — augmented control, model-error cost term, separate
model_err_cov_op (Q).

This epic establishes the foundation. FourDVarNet (Epic 6) and
AmortizedPosterior (Epic 8) are learned variants of these classical
methods.

records.content:
Renamed in v0.4.0 (was IncrementalVarDA).

IncrementalFourDVar is functionally a StrongFourDVar with a
specialised inner solver: Gauss-Newton outer iterations on the full
nonlinear cost, CG / Lanczos inner iterations on the linearised
quadratic subproblem, control-variable transform via
gaussx.MaternLinearOperator.half() for preconditioning.

For users:

Use StrongFourDVar with minimiser=optimistix.NonlinearCG(...) for
general 4DVar problems.

Use IncrementalFourDVar when you want the operational pattern — fewer
outer iterations, exact tangent-linear via jax.linearize, and CG
inner with gaussx-preconditioned Hessian.

The two share ForwardModel, ObservationOperator, and Posterior
contracts. The choice between them is performance-driven, not
semantic — both solve the same minimisation problem.

hierarchy.lvl2: D14: DA hierarchy as horizontal peer classes
D14: DA hierarchy as horizontal peer classes

records.content:
New in v0.4.0.

The previous v0.3 design organised methods into three families —
VarDANet* (learned), IncrementalVarDA* (operational), AmortizedVarDA*
(direct). This was 4DVarNet-centric: it treated the learned method as
the canonical case and the classical methods as historical variants.

The v0.4 design treats classical and learned DA methods as siblings.
Seven peer classes, all implementing pipekit_cycle.AnalysisStep, none
inheriting from any of the others:

Method

Use when

OptimalInterpolation

Linear H, Gaussian B, R. Static field. The right default.

ThreeDVar

Nonlinear H, single time. Snapshot inversion.

StrongFourDVar

Multi-time, control = x_0, model treated as exact.

WeakFourDVar

Multi-time, control = (x_0, \eta_1, \ldots, \eta_T). Model-error-aware.

IncrementalFourDVar

Operational fast path: GN outer + CG inner + CVT (= StrongFourDVar).

FourDVarNet

Learned prior + learned grad modulator. Research, data-rich regimes.

AmortizedPosterior

Direct q_\phi(x \mid y). Real-time / many-event regimes.

Why horizontal.

BLUE / OI is the right tool when the regime allows it. Forcing it
through ThreeDVar with an “isLinear” branch hides the closed-form
fast path and confuses the reader about complexity.

Strong- and weak-constraint 4DVar are different problems (different
control vectors, different cost terms), not configurations of a
single class. Burying them under a mode: Literal["strong", "weak"]
flag obscures the structural difference.

FourDVarNet is one variant of 4DVar with learned components — but it
is not the parent of classical 4DVar. Treating it as such was a
category error inherited from the 4DVarNet-starter codebase.

Apply.

All seven classes live as siblings in vardax/_src/models/.

All seven implement .as_analysis_step() returning the same protocol
shape.

Naming convention: spelled-out names (StrongFourDVar, not
VarDA4DStrong or FourDVarStrong). No VarDA prefix on the class
names — vardax is the package, the classes are named for the
method.

Math reference chapters 4–10 cover one method each, with chapter 1
(problem setting), chapter 2 (observation model), and chapter 3
(dynamical model) supplying the shared foundation.

D15: Lean on optimistix / diffrax adjoints, not in-house grad modes

records.content:
New in v0.4.0.

The v0.3 design defined grad_mode: Literal["unrolled", "one_step", "implicit"] on FourDVarNet* and hand-rolled the three corresponding
differentiation paths in vardax._src.solver. This was useful as a
proof of concept but is the wrong long-term design:

optimistix.AbstractAdjoint already provides
RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint, ImplicitAdjoint, DirectAdjoint for
gradients through minimisers.

diffrax.AbstractAdjoint already provides
RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint, BacksolveAdjoint (continuous adjoint),
ForwardMode, DirectAdjoint for gradients through ODE integration.

Vardax exposes both as constructor slots and delegates the actual
gradient computation upstream:

import diffrax as dfx
import equinox as eqx
import optimistix as optx


# today* (vardax)
class StrongFourDVar(eqx.Module):
    ...
    minimiser: optx.AbstractMinimiser
    # today (optimistix)
    # dx*/dθ = −(∇²ₓJ)⁻¹ ∇²ₓθ J
    minimiser_adjoint: optx.AbstractAdjoint = optx.ImplicitAdjoint()
    # today (diffrax); vardax ships default None (keep the forward's own adjoint)
    forward_adjoint: dfx.AbstractAdjoint = dfx.RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint()

Program 1:Declares the two adjoint slots of StrongFourDVar, one for the analysis that minimises 

(6.1) (via 

(12.2) by default) and one for the rollout 

(1.3).

A user who wants the operational memory profile:

import diffrax as dfx
import optimistix as optx

# today (optimistix)
# dx*/dθ = −(∇²ₓJ)⁻¹ ∇²ₓθ J
minimiser_adjoint = optx.ImplicitAdjoint()
# today (diffrax)
# dλ/dt = −(∂f/∂x)ᵀ λ, integrated backwards
forward_adjoint = dfx.BacksolveAdjoint()

Program 2:Picks the implicit-function adjoint 

(12.2) for the analysis and the continuous adjoint 

(12.1) for the rollout.

A user training FourDVarNet:

import optimistix as optx
import vardax as vdx

# today (optimistix); the FourDVarNet*D slot is named solver_adjoint
# backpropagate through every unrolled step
minimiser_adjoint = optx.RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint()
# or, once contributed upstream:
# today (vardax)
# differentiate the last step only (Bolte et al. 2023)
minimiser_adjoint = vdx.adjoints.OneStepAdjoint()

Program 3:Picks the adjoint that trains FourDVarNet through its unrolled solver 

(9.2) under the loss 

(9.3).

Apply.

Drop GradMode enum from the public API.

Drop unrolled_solve, one_step_solve, implicit_solve as separate
Layer 0 primitives. Their logic moves into the appropriate
optimistix.AbstractAdjoint subclasses.

Bolte 2023 “one-step” differentiation is implemented as
vardax._src.adjoints.one_step.OneStepAdjoint(optimistix.AbstractAdjoint)
with the goal of upstreaming (continues D6).

The continuous adjoint via diffrax.BacksolveAdjoint becomes the
recommended default for memory-constrained 4DVar with long
assimilation windows.

This decision composes with D6: vardax’s novel solver / adjoint
contributions become upstream optimistix / diffrax subclasses, not
parallel in-tree code.

hierarchy.lvl2: D16: BLUE / OI as a first-class method
D16: BLUE / OI as a first-class method

records.content:
New in v0.4.0.

Optimal interpolation (BLUE) — the closed-form linear-Gaussian analysis
— is the first method vardax users should reach for when the regime
permits. It is not a degenerate case of 3DVar to be invoked via an
auto-detected branch; it is its own OptimalInterpolation class with
its own fast path.

The analysis isx^* = x_b + B H^\top (H B H^\top + R)^{-1} (y - H x_b),

with posterior covarianceP^* = B - B H^\top (H B H^\top + R)^{-1} H B = (B^{-1} + H^\top R^{-1} H)^{-1}.

When B, R, H are structured (Matérn, Kronecker, AveragingKernel),
gaussx solves these expressions efficiently without materialising
dense matrices. The whole analysis runs in a handful of structured
mat-vec operations.

Why first-class.

The closed form is exact; no iteration, no convergence criterion, no
adjoint. When applicable it is faster and more accurate than
3DVar’s iterative solution.

The posterior covariance comes for free in the same expression — no
separate PosteriorAdapter call needed.

It is the canonical baseline. Every more sophisticated method must
agree with OI in the linear-Gaussian limit; if it doesn’t, something
is wrong. Making OI a first-class method makes this baseline easy to
produce.

The Kalman filter analysis step is OI. Code reuse between vardax
and ensemble libraries (filterax) is direct.

Apply.

vardax/_src/models/optimal_interpolation.py implements
OptimalInterpolation(eqx.Module) with no minimiser slot.

linearize() is required on the observation operator. If H is
intrinsically nonlinear, the user picks ThreeDVar instead;
OptimalInterpolation.__init__ validates linearity and refuses
nonlinear obs_op.

A new Layer 0 primitive blue_analysis(x_b, y, B_op, R_op, H_op)
implements the closed-form math via gaussx.

Math chapter 4 covers BLUE / OI in detail, including the Sherman–
Morrison–Woodbury identity used to pick between the B-space and
the R-space form.

records.content:
New in v0.5.0.

Latent data assimilation — performing the variational analysis in a
learned low-dimensional latent space \mathcal{Z} — is added as a
peer family of three new Layer-2 classes alongside the seven
established in D14:

LatentThreeDVar — single-time inversion in \mathcal{Z}.

LatentStrongFourDVar — multi-time, latent dynamics M_z.

LatentHybridFourDVar — multi-time, physics forecast in \mathcal{X},
control and background in \mathcal{Z}.

Context. Vardax already uses learned subspaces in three places —
the AE priors inside FourDVarNet*, the observation encoder inside
AmortizedPosterior, and the heads of the amortised family. None of
these promote z itself to the control variable; the variational
problem still solves in \mathcal{X}. The benchmark literature
(Peyron 2021, Cheng 2023, Fablet 2021) consistently shows that
promoting z to control gives an order-of-magnitude wall-clock win
and a structurally smaller posterior covariance.

Options.

(A) Add space: Literal["x", "z"] to existing methods and dispatch
internally.
(B) Add three new peer classes; reuse the AE priors as LatentMaps.
(C) Treat latent DA as a configuration of FourDVarNet.

Decision. Option B.

Rationale.

The control vector (z vs x), the cost dimensionality, the Hessian
object, and the posterior covariance all live in genuinely different
spaces. The D14 pattern argues we should not hide a structural
difference behind a flag.

The AE priors of FourDVarNet are regularisers, not
parameterisations. Conflating regularisation and parameterisation
(Option C) confuses the reader and forces users to thread the
prior slot to mean two different things.

Three peer classes mirror the three flavours formalised in the
pipekit_cycle.LatentDACycle orchestrator: strong (z forecast +
z update), prior-only (x forecast + x update, AE inside cost),
hybrid (x forecast + z update). The vardax peers map 1-to-1 to those
flavours.

Apply.

New module vardax/_src/models/latent.py with the three classes.

New module vardax/_src/latent.py with LatentPrior and
NeuralLatentForwardModel adapter.

Existing BilinAEPrior1D/2D, MLPAEPrior1D, ConvAEPrior1D gain
latent_dim and state_signature properties so they satisfy
pipekit_cycle.LatentMap structurally. No behaviour change.

New Layer-0 primitives variational_cost_latent,
latent_incremental_cost, plus an identity_latent_map(N) helper
for the regression test in §18.6 of the math reference.

New posterior adapter LatentLaplaceCovariance in
vardax/_src/posterior/latent.py.

Math chapter 18 covers the formalism; design doc
design/latent_da.md covers the API.

Consequences.

Three more peers in the Layer-2 family (now ten). D14’s “no
parent–child” rule applies: latent peers do not inherit from
StrongFourDVar or each other.

LatentMap is a substrate-neutral pipekit-cycle protocol, not a
vardax-owned one. Cross-library compatibility with filterax
(LatentETKF, LatentLETKF) is automatic.

WeakLatentFourDVar and a VAE-aware LatentMap are explicitly
deferred to v0.6 (see design/latent_da.md §13).

New in v0.6.0. Resolves #17 (mfourdvar migration, Phase 2).

Dynamics-aware priors ported from mfourdvar (DynIncrements,
DynTrajectory) need the window’s time coordinates; the static


Prior seam (\varphi: x \mapsto x) cannot
express them.

Options.

(A) Widen Prior to __call__(x, ts=None) — one protocol, optional
time.
(B) A separate runtime-checkable TemporalPrior protocol
(__call__(x, ts), loss(x, ts, x_gt=None, params=None)), plus a
bind(ts) bridge returning a Prior-conforming closure.
(C) Batch-carrier signature prior(batch) for all priors.

Decision. Option B.

Rationale.

Time-dependence is a structural difference, not a default-able
argument (same argument as D14/D17: don’t hide structure behind
flags). Widening Prior (A) would make every static-prior call site
carry a vestigial ts.

bind(ts) gives one-way adaptation at zero cost: a bound temporal
prior is a Prior, so variational_cost(x, batch, prior.bind(ts))
turns the prior term into a weak-constraint dynamical residual with
no API change. The reverse direction (a static prior where time is
required) is meaningless, so no two-way adapter exists.

The concrete classes stay eqx.Module (D1); the ODE RHS stays a
plain diffrax-compatible callable — the flax.linen note in the
original issue predates the vardax rewrite.

reconstruct(x, ts) is the shape-preserving map that makes
‖x − reconstruct(x, ts)‖² equal the prior’s own loss, mirroring
the autoencoder-reconstruction semantics of the static seam.

Apply.

TemporalPrior protocol in vardax/_src/protocols.py; satisfied
structurally by DynIncrements / DynTrajectory.

DynamicalPrior.reconstruct / .bind(ts) in
vardax/_src/priors_dynamical.py; bind returns the private
_BoundTemporalPrior (same pattern as .as_analysis_step()).

DynamicalPrior.as_forward_model(dt) adapts the wrapped ODE to
pipekit_cycle.ForwardModel (step / dt / state_signature),
so a dynamical prior can drive StrongFourDVar or a
pipekit_cycle.DACycle directly (D8). step integrates over
[0, dt] — autonomous dynamics assumed.

records.content:
New in v0.6.0. Resolves #18 (mfourdvar migration, Phase 2);
ratifies the API shipped with the Phase-1 port (#60).

The mfourdvar migration introduced a 3-term cost (obs + prior +
background) and a strong-constraint mode where the model propagates
x₀ before the obs term.

Options.

(A) Separate functions: variational_cost (weak, unchanged) +
strong_variational_cost + background_cost helper.
(B) One function with mode="weak" | "strong".
(C) A VarCostConfig dataclass mirroring mfourdvar’s class-based
VariationalCost.

Decision. Option A.

Rationale.

Weak and strong costs have different control variables (full field
x vs initial state x₀) and different required inputs (ts,
forward_fn). A mode flag (B) would bolt two signatures onto one
function and put a Python branch inside jitted code.

The class-based form (C) already exists at Layer 2:
StrongFourDVar / WeakFourDVar are the stateful counterparts.
The functional layer stays flat and composable (matches the
existing obs_cost_* / prior_cost family).

Backward compatible: variational_cost is untouched; NaN handling
is an additive nan_to_num: bool = False kwarg on obs_cost_1d/2d
(chosen over separate *_nan variants to avoid a parallel family —
supersedes the naming sketched in #16), and
strong_variational_cost defaults background = initial_state (no background term)
and weights alpha_obs = alpha_bg = 0.5 to mirror
variational_cost’s convention.

Apply.

All functions live in vardax/_src/costs.py; exported flat from the
package root (D14-style flat namespace — no vardax.dynamical
submodule).

Docstrings carry the constraint-mode math; weak-vs-strong contrast
documented in docs/06_strong_4dvar.md terms.

Layer 1 — Component Examples — Layer 1: implementing Prior,

End-to-end Use Cases — full walkthroughs anchoring the

Implementing protocols and composing eqx.Module operators.

import equinox as eqx
import vardax as vdx
from jaxtyping import Array, Float

# Shapes: T times; N state cells
# Given: enc, dec (eqx.nn.Sequential encoder and decoder)


# user
class ConvAEPrior(eqx.Module):
    """Autoencoder prior φ(x) = dec(enc(x))."""

    encoder: eqx.nn.Sequential
    decoder: eqx.nn.Sequential

    def __call__(self, x: Float[Array, "T N"]) -> Float[Array, "T N"]:
        # z = enc(x)
        latent = self.encoder(x)
        # φ(x) = dec(z)
        return self.decoder(latent)


# today (vardax)
# Structural conformance, no inheritance needed (runtime-checkable Protocol)
assert isinstance(ConvAEPrior(enc, dec), vdx.Prior)

Program 1:Implements an autoencoder prior φ for the learned prior term of the 4DVarNet cost 

(9.1) and checks it against the Prior protocol.

Vardax obs operators satisfy pipekit_cycle.ObservationOperator
directly (Decision D8). Implement both __call__ and linearize:

import equinox as eqx
import lineax as lx
import pipekit_cycle as pc
from jaxtyping import Array, Float

# Shapes: N state cells


# user
class MaskedIdentity(eqx.Module):
    """H(x) = mask ⊙ x."""

    def __call__(
        self, x: Float[Array, " N"], mask: Float[Array, " N"] | None = None
    ) -> Float[Array, " N"]:
        # H(x) = m ⊙ x, or x when no mask is given
        return x * mask if mask is not None else x

    def linearize(self, x: Float[Array, " N"]) -> lx.AbstractLinearOperator:
        # today (lineax)
        # H′(x) = ∂H/∂x
        return lx.JacobianLinearOperator(self.__call__, x)  # (N, N) op


# today (pipekit_cycle)
assert isinstance(MaskedIdentity(), pc.ObservationOperator)

Program 2:Implements the masked-identity operator 

(2.3) with a Jacobian linearisation and checks it against the pipekit_cycle protocol.

import lineax as lx
import vardax as vdx

# Shapes: N levels
# Given: A_matrix (N, N), retrieval_prior x_a (N,), weighting_vector h (N,),
#        state x (N,), residual r (N,)

# today (lineax)
# A, or a gaussx structured operator
kernel_op = lx.MatrixLinearOperator(A_matrix)  # (N, N) op
# today (vardax)
ak = vdx.AveragingKernel(
    kernel_matrix=kernel_op,
    prior_profile=retrieval_prior,
    pressure_weights=weighting_vector,
)

# today (vardax)
# ŷ = A (h ⊙ x + (1 − h) ⊙ x_a)
y_pred = ak(x)  # (N,) → (N,)

# Tangent-linear operator for incremental 4DVar
# today (vardax)
# H′ = A diag(h)
obs_jacobian = ak.linearize(x)  # (N,) → (N, N) op
# today (lineax)
# H′ᵀ
obs_adjoint = obs_jacobian.transpose()  # (N, N) op
# today (lineax)
# H′ᵀ r
y_adjoint = obs_adjoint.mv(residual)  # (N,) → (N,)

Program 3:Applies the averaging-kernel operator 

(2.5) and its tangent-linear adjoint, the pair checked by 

(2.7).

import lineax as lx
import pipekit_cycle as pc
import vardax as vdx

# Shapes: N state cells; Mᵢ observations of instrument i
# Given: tropomi_A, tropomi_xa, tropomi_h, tropomi_qa_flag,
#        tropomi_uncertainty (Mᵢ,), state x (N,), batch

# today (vardax)
# Hᵢ(x) = Aᵢ (hᵢ ⊙ x + (1 − hᵢ) ⊙ x_a,i)
tropomi_ak = vdx.AveragingKernel(
    kernel_matrix=tropomi_A, prior_profile=tropomi_xa, pressure_weights=tropomi_h
)
# today (lineax)
# Rᵢ = diag(σᵢ²)
tropomi_cov = lx.DiagonalLinearOperator(tropomi_uncertainty)  # (Mᵢ, Mᵢ) op
# today (vardax)
# (Hᵢ, mᵢ, Rᵢ) for i = TROPOMI
tropomi_spec = vdx.InstrumentSpec(
    obs_op=tropomi_ak,
    mask=tropomi_qa_flag,
    obs_cov_op=tropomi_cov,
    instrument_id="TROPOMI",
)
# today* (vardax)
emit_spec = vdx.InstrumentSpec(...)
# today* (vardax)
ghgsat_spec = vdx.InstrumentSpec(...)

# today (vardax)
registry = vdx.InstrumentRegistry(
    entries={
        "TROPOMI": tropomi_spec,
        "EMIT": emit_spec,
        "GHGSat": ghgsat_spec,
    }
)
# today (vardax)
fusion = vdx.MultiInstrumentFusion(registry=registry)

# Returns dict[instrument_id, predicted_obs]
# today* (vardax; __call__ takes the state only)
# {i: Hᵢ(x)}
predictions = fusion(x, batch)  # (N,) → {i: (Mᵢ,)}

# For strict pipekit_cycle.ObservationOperator contexts, use the adapter:
# today (vardax)
# H(x) = [H_TROPOMI(x); H_EMIT(x); H_GHGSat(x)]
fusion_as_op = fusion.to_observation_operator()
# today (pipekit_cycle)
assert isinstance(fusion_as_op, pc.ObservationOperator)

Program 4:Builds the multi-instrument operator behind the fusion cost 

(2.6) from per-instrument averaging kernels 

(2.5).

import equinox as eqx
import vardax as vdx
from jaxtyping import Array, Float

# Shapes: C channels; G hidden channels; H × W grid
# Given: lstm (a ConvLSTM cell), proj (an eqx.nn.Conv2d from G to C channels)

Carry = tuple[Float[Array, "G H W"], Float[Array, "G H W"]]


# user
class ConvLSTMGradMod(eqx.Module):
    """Φ(∇ₓJ, h) → (update, h′) with a ConvLSTM cell and a projection."""

    conv_lstm: eqx.Module
    output_proj: eqx.nn.Conv2d

    def __call__(
        self, grad: Float[Array, "C H W"], carry: Carry
    ) -> tuple[Float[Array, "C H W"], Carry]:
        hidden, cell = carry
        # (h′, c′) = ConvLSTM(∇ₓJ, (h, c))
        hidden, cell = self.conv_lstm(grad, (hidden, cell))
        # Φ(∇ₓJ, h) = W h′
        update = self.output_proj(hidden)
        return update, (hidden, cell)


# today* (vardax; the shipped protocol is __call__(grad, state, carry))
assert isinstance(ConvLSTMGradMod(lstm, proj), vdx.GradModulator)

Program 5:Implements the learned gradient modulator Φ of the 4DVarNet update 

(9.2) as a ConvLSTM.

The grad modulator family is FourDVarNet-specific. Classical methods
use optimistix.AbstractMinimiser for the inner solver instead.

import optimistix as optx
import vardax as vdx

# Given: obs_op, background x_b, prior_cov B op, obs_cov R op

# Pick any optimistix minimiser
# proposed (D6; vdx.Minimiser ships as a Protocol, the wrapper is
#   vdx.OptimistixMinimiser(solver), with no adjoint field)
gn = vdx.Minimiser(
    optx.GaussNewton(rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-5), adjoint=optx.ImplicitAdjoint()
)
# proposed (D6)
bfgs = vdx.Minimiser(optx.BFGS(rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-5))
# proposed (D6)
ncg = vdx.Minimiser(optx.NonlinearCG(rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-5))

# today* (vardax; gn.minimiser and gn.adjoint are proposed)
# x* = argmin J(x)
model = vdx.ThreeDVar(
    obs_op=obs_op,
    prior_mean=background,
    prior_cov_op=prior_cov,
    obs_cov_op=obs_cov,
    # the underlying optimistix solver
    minimiser=gn.minimiser,
    minimiser_adjoint=gn.adjoint,
)

Program 6:Wraps optimistix minimisers for the 3DVar cost 

(5.1) and passes one to ThreeDVar.

The Minimiser wrapper is convenience; you can also pass the
optimistix.AbstractMinimiser directly into the model constructor.

import gaussx as gx
import lineax as lx
import vardax as vdx

# Shapes: S windows; N state cells; M observations; D = 2 coordinates
# Given: H_lin_op (M, N) lineax op, background x_b (N,), coords (N, D),
#        obs_uncertainty (M,), batch

# today (vardax)
# H(x) = H x, must be linear
obs_op = vdx.LinearObs(operator=H_lin_op)
# proposed (gaussx)
# Bᵢⱼ = k_Matérn(sᵢ, sⱼ; ℓ = 10, σ = 0.1)
prior_cov = gx.MaternLinearOperator(  # (N, D) → (N, N) PSD op
    coords, length_scale=10.0, sigma=0.1
)
# today (lineax)
# R = diag(σ²)
obs_cov = lx.DiagonalLinearOperator(obs_uncertainty)  # (M,) → (M, M) op

# today (vardax)
model = vdx.OptimalInterpolation(
    obs_op=obs_op,
    prior_mean=background,
    prior_cov_op=prior_cov,
    obs_cov_op=obs_cov,
)

# today (vardax)
# closed form: x* = x_b + K (y − H x_b)
analysis = model(batch)  # → (S, N)
# today (vardax)
# closed form: P* = (I − K H) B, with mean and provenance
posterior = model.posterior(batch)  # Posterior(mean (N,), cov (N, N) op)

import optimistix as optx
import vardax as vdx

# Shapes: S windows; N levels

obs_op = vdx.AveragingKernel(kernel_matrix=A, prior_profile=xa, pressure_weights=h)

#   AbstractMinimiser, so the model rejects it: use optx.BFGS or NonlinearCG)
# J(x) = ½ ‖x − x_b‖²_{B⁻¹} + ½ ‖y − H(x)‖²_{R⁻¹}
model = vdx.ThreeDVar(
    obs_op=obs_op,
    prior_mean=background,
    prior_cov_op=prior_cov,
    obs_cov_op=obs_cov,
    minimiser=optx.GaussNewton(rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-5),
    minimiser_adjoint=optx.ImplicitAdjoint(),
)
# today (vardax)
# x* = argmin J(x)
analysis = model(batch)  # → (S, N)

import diffrax as dfx
import vardax as vdx

# Shapes: S windows; T times; N state cells
# Given: somax_model, A (N, N) lineax op, xa x_a (N,), h (N,),
#        background x_b (N,), prior_cov B op, obs_cov R op, batch

# today (vardax)
# ŷ = A (h ⊙ x + (1 − h) ⊙ x_a)
obs_op = vdx.AveragingKernel(kernel_matrix=A, prior_profile=xa, pressure_weights=h)

# today (vardax)
# 3 outer relinearisations, 20 CG steps each, in χ with x₀ − x_b = S χ
model = vdx.IncrementalFourDVar(
    forward=somax_model,
    obs_op=obs_op,
    prior_mean=background,
    prior_cov_op=prior_cov,
    obs_cov_op=obs_cov,
    config=vdx.IncrementalConfig(n_outer=3, n_inner=20, cvt=True),
    forward_adjoint=dfx.BacksolveAdjoint(),
)

# today (vardax)
# x₀* after the last outer iteration
analysis = model(batch)  # → (S, N)
# today (vardax)
# P*_GN = 𝐇_GN⁻¹, reusing the Hessian of the last outer iteration
posterior = model.posterior(batch)  # Posterior(mean (N,), cov (N, N) op)

(8.3) in control variables

import vardax as vdx

# Shapes: K = 15 inner steps
# Given: enc, dec, lstm, proj, and the page's ConvAEPrior, MaskedIdentity and
#        ConvLSTMGradMod

# proposed (D14; ships today as vdx.FourDVarNet1D / vdx.FourDVarNet2D)
# x_{k+1} = x_k − Φ(∇ₓJ(x_k), h_k), k = 0 … K − 1
model = vdx.FourDVarNet(
    prior=ConvAEPrior(encoder=enc, decoder=dec),
    obs_op=MaskedIdentity(),
    grad_mod=ConvLSTMGradMod(lstm, proj),

(9.2).

import vardax as vdx

# Shapes: N state cells
# Given: strong_4dvar, oi, incremental (built as above), batch

# Classical: pair with explicit adapter
# today (vardax)
# x₀* = argmin J(x₀)
analysis = strong_4dvar(batch)  # → (S, N)

posterior = vdx.LaplaceCovariance()(analysis, strong_4dvar.as_analysis_step(), batch)

posterior = oi.posterior(batch)

mark_likelihood = vdx.GaussianMarkLikelihood(
    posterior=posterior,

import somax
import vardax as vdx

# Shapes: N state cells; K = 15 inner steps
# Given: grid, params, background x_b (N,), prior_cov B op, obs_cov R op

# not pinned (somax)

    prior=prior,

    config=vdx.SolverConfig(n_steps=15),
)

# today (vardax)

incremental = vdx.IncrementalFourDVar(
    forward=swm,
    obs_op=vdx.MaskedIdentity(),
    prior_mean=background,
    prior_cov_op=prior_cov,
    obs_cov_op=obs_cov,

import gaussx as gx
import lineax as lx
import plumax
import vardax as vdx

# Shapes: P = 4 source parameters (Q, x₀, y₀, H_eff); Mᵢ observations of instrument i
# Given: met_field, tropomi_l2_ds, emit_l2_ds, ghgsat_l2_ds (L2 datasets),
#        Q_prior_mean (P,), Q_prior_mu, Q_prior_sigma_log, batch

# not pinned (plumax)
# F(Q, x₀, u, θ) = predicted XCH4 enhancement
plume_fwd = plumax.tier1.GaussianPlume(met=met_field, dispersion="MO")

# Observation: averaging kernel from TROPOMI L2 metadata
# proposed (D9)
# ŷ = A (h ⊙ x + (1 − h) ⊙ x_a), with A, h, x_a read from the L2 file
tropomi_ak = vdx.AveragingKernel.from_l2(tropomi_l2_ds)

# Multi-instrument fusion (per-instrument bias as joint state, Epic 9)
# proposed (D9)
registry = vdx.InstrumentRegistry.from_l2_dict(
    {
        "TROPOMI": tropomi_l2_ds,
        "EMIT": emit_l2_ds,
        "GHGSat": ghgsat_l2_ds,
    }
)
# today (vardax)
# J_obs(x) = Σᵢ αᵢ ½ ‖mᵢ ⊙ (yᵢ − Hᵢ(x))‖²_{Rᵢ⁻¹}
fusion = vdx.MultiInstrumentFusion(registry=registry)

# proposed (gaussx)
# log Q ~ 𝒩(μ, σ²)
prior_cov = gx.LogNormalLinearOperator(Q_prior_mu, Q_prior_sigma_log)  # (P, P) op
# proposed (lineax; gaussx ships gx.BlockDiag(*operators))
# R = blockdiag(R_TROPOMI, R_EMIT, R_GHGSat)
obs_cov = lx.BlockDiagonalLinearOperator(  # (Σ Mᵢ, Σ Mᵢ) op
    [spec.obs_cov_op for spec in fusion.registry.entries.values()]
)

# Invert
# today* (vardax; a fused obs_op goes in as fusion.to_observation_operator())
# δJ(δx) over the source parameters
inversion = vdx.IncrementalFourDVar(
    forward=plume_fwd,
    obs_op=fusion,
    prior_mean=Q_prior_mean,
    prior_cov_op=prior_cov,
    obs_cov_op=obs_cov,
    config=vdx.IncrementalConfig(n_outer=3, n_inner=20),
)

# today (vardax)
# x* after the last outer iteration
analysis = inversion(batch)  # → (1, P)
# today* (vardax; the adapter takes one window's analysis, e.g. analysis[0])
# P*_GN = 𝐇_GN⁻¹ at x*
posterior = vdx.GaussNewtonHessian()(analysis, inversion.as_analysis_step(), batch)

import gaussx as gx

# Shapes: N = N_lon × N_lat grid cells; D = 2 coordinates
# Given: coords (N, D), lon (N_lon,), lat (N_lat,)

# Matérn-3/2 on a regular grid, supports Kronecker structure
# proposed (gaussx)
# Bᵢⱼ = k_Matérn-3/2(sᵢ, sⱼ; ℓ = 10 km, σ = 1)
prior_cov = gx.MaternLinearOperator(  # (N, D) → (N, N) PSD op
    grid_coords=coords,
    # km, basin-dependent
    length_scale=10.0,
    # Matérn-3/2
    nu=1.5,
    sigma=1.0,
)

# Returns B^{1/2} for CVT
# proposed (gaussx; gaussx ships gx.sqrt(operator))
# S = B^{1/2}
prior_sqrt = prior_cov.half()  # (N, N) op

# Or a Kronecker product (separable in lon/lat):
# proposed (gaussx)
# B_lon, ℓ = 5
lon_cov = gx.Matern1DLinearOperator(coords=lon, length_scale=5.0)  # (N_lon, N_lon) op
# proposed (gaussx)
# B_lat, ℓ = 3
lat_cov = gx.Matern1DLinearOperator(coords=lat, length_scale=3.0)  # (N_lat, N_lat) op
# proposed (gaussx; gaussx ships gx.Kronecker)
# B = B_lon ⊗ B_lat
kron_cov = gx.KroneckerLinearOperator([lon_cov, lat_cov])  # (N, N) op

import einx
import filterax as fx
import jax
import vardax as vdx

# Shapes: E = 32 members; N state cells
# Given: somax_model, background x_b (N,), state_shape = (N,), B_climatological op,
#        fusion, obs_cov R op, batch

key_perturb = jax.random.PRNGKey(0)

# δx⁽ᵉ⁾ ~ 𝒩(0, I)
initial_perturbations = jax.random.normal(key_perturb, (32, *state_shape))  # (E, N)

# Ensemble forecast (filterax owns this)
# not pinned (filterax)
ensemble_forecast = fx.EnsembleForecast(
    forward=somax_model,
    n_members=32,
    initial_perturbations=initial_perturbations,
)
# not pinned (filterax)
# x⁽ᵉ⁾ = M(x_b + δx⁽ᵉ⁾)
ensemble_states = ensemble_forecast(background)  # (N,) → (E, N)

# Hybrid B: blend climatological + ensemble
# not pinned (filterax)
# P_ens = 1/(E − 1) Σₑ (x⁽ᵉ⁾ − x̄)(x⁽ᵉ⁾ − x̄)ᵀ
ensemble_cov = fx.ensemble_covariance(ensemble_states)  # (E, N) → (N, N) op
# B_hybrid = ½ B_clim + ½ P_ens
hybrid_cov = 0.5 * B_climatological + 0.5 * ensemble_cov  # (N, N) op
# x̄ = 1/E Σₑ x⁽ᵉ⁾
ensemble_mean = einx.mean("e n -> n", ensemble_states)  # (E, N) → (N,)

# Run vardax inversion with hybrid B
# today* (vardax; a fused obs_op goes in as fusion.to_observation_operator())
# δJ(δx) with B = B_hybrid
model = vdx.IncrementalFourDVar(
    forward=somax_model,
    obs_op=fusion,
    prior_mean=ensemble_mean,
    prior_cov_op=hybrid_cov,
    obs_cov_op=obs_cov,
    config=vdx.IncrementalConfig(),
)
# today (vardax)
# x₀* after the last outer iteration
analysis = model(batch)  # → (S, N)

# Posterior from the ensemble itself
# today (vardax)
# P*_ens from the E members
posterior = vdx.EnsembleCovariance(n_members=32)(
    ensemble_states, model.as_analysis_step(), batch
)

import jax
import vardax as vdx

# Shapes: S windows; T times; N state cells
# Given: state x (S, T, N), batch (y, m), obs_op H, obs_precision R⁻¹ op,
#        background x_b, prior_precision B⁻¹ op, ae_prior φ

# proposed (D19)
# J_obs(x) = ½ ‖m ⊙ (y − H(x))‖²_{R⁻¹}
obs_term = vdx.obs_cost(  # → ()
    state, batch.input, batch.mask, obs_operator=obs_op, R_inv_op=obs_precision
)

# today* (vardax)
# J_b(x) = ½ ‖x − x_b‖²_{B⁻¹}
prior_term_classical = vdx.prior_cost(  # → ()
    state, prior_mean=background, B_inv_op=prior_precision
)

# today* (vardax)
# J_prior(x) = ‖x − φ(x)‖²
prior_term_learned = vdx.prior_cost(state, prior_fn=ae_prior)  # → ()

# today* (vardax)
# J(x) = α_obs ½ ‖H(x) − y‖²_{R⁻¹} + α_prior ‖x − φ(x)‖²
total_cost = vdx.variational_cost(  # → ()
    state,
    batch,
    prior_fn=ae_prior,
    obs_operator=obs_op,
    alpha_obs=1.0,
    alpha_prior=0.1,
)

# today* (vardax)
# ∇ₓJ(x)
cost_grad = jax.grad(vdx.variational_cost)(  # (S, T, N)
    state, batch, ae_prior, obs_op, 1.0, 0.1
)

#        initial_state, prior_cov B, obs_cov R and config for the helper


# user
def step(state: Float[Array, " N"]) -> Float[Array, " N"]:
    """One model step Mₜ(x) of the forward."""
    return forward_model.step(state, dt)


# Mₜ(x_b + δx) ≈ Mₜ(x_b) + M′ₜ δx

# today (vardax)
# Hₜ(z + δz) ≈ Hₜ(z) + H′ₜ δz
obs_op_lin = obs_op.linearize(background)  # (N,) → (M, N) op
# δx⁽⁰⁾ = 0

    obs_op_lin=obs_op_lin,
    B_inv_op=prior_precision,
    R_inv_op=obs_precision,
    n_inner=20,
    cg_atol=1e-5,
    cg_rtol=1e-5,
)

# x⁽ᵏ⁺¹⁾ = x⁽ᵏ⁾ + δx*
background = background + increment  # (N,)

# proposed (D11)
# x* after config.n_outer relinearisations
analysis = vdx.solver.incremental_outer(  # (N,)
    initial_state, batch, forward_model, obs_op, prior_cov, obs_cov, config

    minimiser_adjoint=optx.ImplicitAdjoint(),

)

model = vdx.StrongFourDVar(
    ...,
    minimiser_adjoint=optx.RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint(),
    forward_adjoint=dfx.RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint(),
)

# today (diffrax)
# forward sensitivity, good when the parameter count is far below N
forward_adjoint = dfx.ForwardMode()

# Shapes: K = 15 inner steps
# Given: ae_prior φ, obs_op H, conv_lstm Φ

# today (vardax)

Methane single-overpass MAP — plumax Tier I + vardax MAP + averaging

Goal. Given multi-instrument satellite observations of an XCH₄
enhancement, estimate the source rate Q, location x_0, and effective
stack height H_\text{eff} for a known facility. Single overpass.

Tier. Plumax Tier I (Gaussian plume / puff).

import gaussx as gx
import geotoolz
import jax.numpy as jnp
import lineax as lx
import plumax
import vardax as vdx

# Shapes: P = 4 source parameters (log Q, x₀, y₀, H_eff); Mᵢ observations of
#         instrument i
# Given: event (facility, time, geometry), edgar_lookup, load_era5_at

# (1) Load satellite + met
# not pinned (geotoolz)
catalog = geotoolz.GeoCatalog.from_geoparquet("s3://catalog/overpasses.parquet")
# not pinned (geotoolz)
overpasses = catalog.query(
    geometry=event.bbox(buffer_km=50),
    interval=event.window(hours=2),
    instruments=["TROPOMI", "EMIT", "GHGSat"],
    quality_min="usable",
)
# user
met = load_era5_at(event.time, event.bbox)

# (2) Forward model: Tier I Gaussian plume
# not pinned (plumax)
plume = plumax.tier1.GaussianPlume(met=met, dispersion="MO")

# (3) Multi-instrument observation operator
# proposed (D9)
registry = vdx.InstrumentRegistry.from_l2_dict(
    {op.instrument: op.l2_ds for op in overpasses}
)
# today (vardax)
# J_obs(x) = Σᵢ αᵢ ½ ‖mᵢ ⊙ (yᵢ − Hᵢ(x))‖²_{Rᵢ⁻¹}
fusion = vdx.MultiInstrumentFusion(registry=registry)

# (4) Prior: lognormal on Q from EDGAR inventory
# user
inventory_rate = edgar_lookup(event.facility_id)  # → ()
# μ = log Q_EDGAR
log_rate_prior_mean = jnp.log(inventory_rate)  # → ()
# σ = 1, a coefficient of variation of about 100%
log_rate_prior_std = 1.0
# proposed (gaussx)
# log Q ~ 𝒩(μ, σ²)
prior_cov = gx.LogNormalLinearOperator(
    mu=log_rate_prior_mean, sigma=log_rate_prior_std
)  # (P, P) op

# (5) Block-diag R across instruments
# proposed (lineax; gaussx ships gx.BlockDiag(*operators))
# R = blockdiag(R_TROPOMI, R_EMIT, R_GHGSat)
obs_cov = lx.BlockDiagonalLinearOperator(  # (Σ Mᵢ, Σ Mᵢ) op
    [spec.obs_cov_op for spec in fusion.registry.entries.values()]
)

# (6) Configure inversion
# x_b = (log Q_EDGAR, 0, 0, 50 m) for (Q, x₀, y₀, H)
prior_mean = jnp.array([log_rate_prior_mean, 0.0, 0.0, 50.0])  # (P,)
# today* (vardax; a fused obs_op goes in as fusion.to_observation_operator())
# δJ(δx) over the source parameters, in χ with x − x_b = S χ
inversion = vdx.IncrementalFourDVar(
    forward=plume,
    obs_op=fusion,
    prior_mean=prior_mean,
    prior_cov_op=prior_cov,
    obs_cov_op=obs_cov,
    config=vdx.IncrementalConfig(n_outer=5, n_inner=20, cvt=True),
)

# (7) Build batch from overpasses
# proposed (no issue yet)
batch = vdx.utils.build_event_batch(overpasses, met=met)

# (8) Invert
# today (vardax)
# x* after the last outer iteration
analysis = inversion(batch)  # → (1, P)

# (9) Posterior via Gauss-Newton Hessian (reuses last GN outer iteration)
# today* (vardax; the adapter takes one window's analysis, e.g. analysis[0])
# P*_GN = 𝐇_GN⁻¹ at x*, from 50 Lanczos vectors
posterior = vdx.GaussNewtonHessian(n_krylov=50)(
    analysis, inversion.as_analysis_step(), batch
)

# (10) Export to population layer (Tier V)
# today (vardax)
mark = vdx.GaussianMarkLikelihood(
    posterior=posterior,
    event_metadata={
        "event_id": event.id,
        "time": event.time,
        "geometry": event.geometry,
        "instruments_used": list(fusion.registry.entries),
        "met_source": "era5_2024-01-15T12Z",
    },
)
# today (vardax)
mark_record = mark.to_dict()
# not pinned (geotoolz)
catalog.write_posterior(event.id, mark_record)

import equinox as eqx
import optax
import pipekit_cycle as pc
import pipekit_experiment
import vardax as vdx

# Shapes: B batch; T = 10 times; H × W = 128 × 128 grid; K = 15 inner steps
# Given: oceanbench_loader, somax_shallow_water, load_altika_stream, n_windows,
#        initial_state, batch

# (1) Build model
# proposed (D14; ships today as vdx.FourDVarNet2D(n_time, height, width, ..., key))
# x_{k+1} = x_k − Φ(∇ₓJ(x_k), h_k), k = 0 … K − 1
model = vdx.FourDVarNet(
    # today* (vardax; also takes key)
    prior=vdx.BilinAEPrior2D(latent_dim=128, n_time=10, height=128, width=128),
    obs_op=vdx.MaskedIdentity(),
    # today* (vardax; also takes key)
    grad_mod=vdx.ConvLSTMGradMod2D(state_channels=10, hidden_dim=64),
    # proposed (D4)
    config=vdx.SolverConfig(n_steps=15, alpha=0.2),
    # O(1) memory training
    solver_adjoint=vdx.adjoints.OneStepAdjoint(),
)

# (2) Training (OceanBench SSH benchmark)
# today (optax)
optimizer = optax.adam(1e-3)
opt_state = optimizer.init(eqx.filter(model, eqx.is_array))

for epoch in range(100):
    for batch in oceanbench_loader:
        # today (vardax)
        # ℒ(θ, φ) = E ‖x*(θ, φ; y) − x_true‖²
        model, opt_state, loss = vdx.train_step(model, batch, optimizer, opt_state)

# (3) Persist via pipekit (Decision D13)
# not pinned (pipekit_experiment)
registry = pipekit_experiment.LocalModelRegistry(root="./ssh_models")
# proposed (D13)
hash_ = vdx.persist.save(model, registry, tags={"task": "ssh_oceanbench"})

# (4) Operational cycling on streaming altimetry
# today (pipekit_cycle)
da_cycle = pc.DACycle(
    # physics oracle for comparison
    forward_model=somax_shallow_water,
    obs_op=model.obs_op,
    analysis_step=model.as_analysis_step(),
    obs_source=load_altika_stream,
    n_steps=n_windows,
)

# (5) Posterior for downstream uncertainty propagation
# today (vardax)
posterior_adapter = vdx.LaplaceCovariance()
# today (pipekit_cycle)
result, final_state = da_cycle(initial_state, pc.DAState(t=0.0, cycle_count=0))
# today* (vardax; the adapter takes one window's analysis, not the cycle result)
# P*_Laplace = (B⁻¹ + H′ᵀ R⁻¹ H′)⁻¹
posterior = posterior_adapter(result, model.as_analysis_step(), batch)

# today (vardax)

vdx.assert_posterior_agreement(p_learned, p_incremental, tolerance_sigma=1.0)

Chapter 18 — Latent Variational DA.

Vardax today exposes three points where a learned subspace already
helps:

BilinAEPrior1D/2D, MLPAEPrior1D, ConvAEPrior1D — autoencoder
priors used inside the cost of FourDVarNet* to regularise the
reconstruction.

AmortizedPosterior.MLPObsEncoder — encodes (y, mask) into a
context vector before the head produces q_\phi(x \mid y).

RegressionHead, ConditionalFlowHead, ScoreDiffusionHead — heads
whose internal state lives implicitly in a low-dim representation.

What is missing is the natural variational counterpart of these:
solving the variational problem itself in latent space. The
benchmark literature (Peyron et al. 2021, Cheng et al. 2023, Fablet
et al. 2021) consistently reports order-of-magnitude wall-clock wins on
this exact reformulation. Vardax should offer it as a peer family of
AnalysisStep classes, not as a per-method retrofit.

For state x \in \mathbb{R}^{N_x}, observations y, autoencoder
(\varphi, \psi), latent dynamics M_z, and lifted operator
\tilde{H} = H \circ \psi:

Latent 3DVar — find z^* = \arg\min_z J_{3D}(z) withJ_{3D}(z) = \tfrac{1}{2}\|z - z_b\|^2_{\mathbf{B}_z^{-1}}
          + \tfrac{1}{2}\|y - H(\psi(z))\|^2_{\mathbf{R}^{-1}}.

Analysis: x^* = \psi(z^*).

Latent Strong-4DVar — control z_0, rollout z_{k+1} = M_z(z_k):J_{4D}(z_0) = \tfrac{1}{2}\|z_0 - z_b\|^2_{\mathbf{B}_z^{-1}}
            + \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{k=0}^{K}\|y_k - H(\psi(z_k))\|^2_{\mathbf{R}^{-1}}.

Latent Hybrid 4DVar — control z_0, decode once to seed the
physical state, then roll out x_{k+1} = M_x(x_k) entirely in
\mathcal{X}; observation residual evaluated on x_k:J_{H}(z_0) = \tfrac{1}{2}\|z_0 - z_b\|^2_{\mathbf{B}_z^{-1}}
           + \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{k=0}^{K}\|y_k - H(x_k)\|^2_{\mathbf{R}^{-1}},
\quad
x_0 = \psi(z_0),\;\; x_{k+1} = M_x(x_k).

In all three, the cost is smaller-dim (N_z \ll N_x), the
minimiser converges faster, and the Hessian / Laplace approximation
lives in \mathcal{Z}. Gradients flow through \psi via JAX autodiff
for eqx.Module decoders — no hand-coded adjoint.

Full derivations, tangent-linear forms, and the Sherman–Morrison–
Woodbury identity used to switch between \mathbf{B}_z-space and
\mathbf{R}-space gain formulas live in the math reference

import einx
import equinox as eqx
import lineax as lx
import pipekit_cycle as pc
from jaxtyping import Array, Float

# Shapes: Nx = state size; Nz = latent size, Nz ≪ Nx


# proposed (D17)
class LatentPrior(eqx.Module):
    """Variational prior in latent space; wraps a LatentMap with B_z.

    Used as the prior term in latent variational costs:

        J_prior(z) = 1/2 (z - z_b)^T B_z^{-1} (z - z_b).
    """

    # today (pipekit_cycle)
    latent_map: pc.LatentMap
    z_b: Float[Array, " Nz"]
    # B_z itself, NOT its inverse
    B_z_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator

    def cost(self, z: Float[Array, " Nz"]) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        # B_z_op is the covariance operator, so a solve applies B_z⁻¹; a
        # precision operator should be wrapped in
        # `lineax.TaggedLinearOperator(B_z_inv, lx.tags.symmetric)` and
        # adapted to a `lineax.matmul`-based cost instead.
        # d = z − z_b
        residual = z - self.z_b  # (Nz,) → (Nz,)
        # B_z⁻¹ d
        whitened = lx.linear_solve(self.B_z_op, residual).value  # (Nz,) → (Nz,)
        # dᵀ B_z⁻¹ d
        quadratic = einx.dot("z, z ->", residual, whitened)  # → ()
        # J_prior(z) = ½ dᵀ B_z⁻¹ d
        return 0.5 * quadratic

    def encode(self, x: Float[Array, " Nx"]) -> Float[Array, " Nz"]:
        # today (pipekit_cycle)
        # z = φ(x)
        return self.latent_map.encode(x)

    def decode(self, z: Float[Array, " Nz"]) -> Float[Array, " Nx"]:
        # today (pipekit_cycle)
        # x = ψ(z)
        return self.latent_map.decode(z)

from typing import Any

import equinox as eqx
from jaxtyping import Array, Float

# Shapes: Nx = state size; Nz = latent size


# today* (vardax); ships __call__ only, with no encode / decode / properties
class MLPAEPrior1D(eqx.Module):
    encoder: eqx.nn.MLP
    decoder: eqx.nn.MLP
    _latent_dim: int = eqx.field(static=True)
    _state_signature: Any = eqx.field(static=True, default=None)

    # proposed (D17): extracted halves of the existing __call__.
    # z = φ(x)
    def encode(self, x: Float[Array, " Nx"]) -> Float[Array, " Nz"]:
        return self.encoder(x)

    # proposed (D17)
    # x = ψ(z)
    def decode(self, z: Float[Array, " Nz"]) -> Float[Array, " Nx"]:
        return self.decoder(z)

    # today (vardax): existing, preserved bit-for-bit.
    # x̂ = ψ(φ(x))
    def __call__(self, x: Float[Array, " Nx"]) -> Float[Array, " Nx"]:
        latent = self.encode(x)  # (Nx,) → (Nz,)
        return self.decode(latent)

    # proposed (D17): make the AE satisfy pipekit_cycle.LatentMap structurally.
    @property
    def latent_dim(self) -> int:
        return self._latent_dim

    # proposed (D17)
    @property
    def state_signature(self) -> Any:
        return self._state_signature

Wraps an eqx.Module that produces z_{k+1} = M_z(z_k). The vast
majority of latent dynamics in the literature is one of three things:

A residual MLP M_z(z) = z + f_\theta(z),

A neural ODE integrated by diffrax,

A learned linear operator (for short horizons).

Rather than ship any one of these (per the user’s earlier decision —
“no, leave to users”), we ship the adapter:

import equinox as eqx
import lineax as lx
import optimistix as optx
import pipekit_cycle as pc
import vardax as vdx
from jaxtyping import Array, Float

# Shapes: Nx = state size; Nz = latent size; D = observations


# proposed (D17)
class LatentThreeDVar(eqx.Module):
    """Latent 3DVar: minimise J_3D(z) over z, decode to x."""

    # today (pipekit_cycle)
    latent_map: pc.LatentMap
    # today (pipekit_cycle); x-space
    obs_op: pc.ObservationOperator
    # proposed (D17)
    prior: LatentPrior
    obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    # today (optimistix)
    minimiser: optx.AbstractMinimiser = optx.BFGS(rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-6)
    # today (optimistix)
    minimiser_adjoint: optx.AbstractAdjoint = optx.ImplicitAdjoint()

    # today (vardax): Batch1D, Batch2D
    def __call__(self, batch: vdx.Batch1D | vdx.Batch2D) -> Float[Array, " Nx"]:
        obs = batch.input
        mask = batch.mask
        # proposed (pipekit-cycle latent.md)
        # H̃ = H ∘ ψ
        lifted_obs_op = pc.LiftedObservationOperator(
            decoder=self.latent_map,
            inner=self.obs_op,
        )

        def cost_fn(z: Float[Array, " Nz"], args: None) -> Float[Array, ""]:
            # H̃(z) = H(ψ(z))
            obs_pred = lifted_obs_op(z)  # (Nz,) → (D,)
            # proposed (D17)
            # J_3D(z) = ½‖z − z_b‖²_{B_z⁻¹} + ½‖y − H(ψ(z))‖²_{R⁻¹}
            return variational_cost_latent(  # → ()
                z=z,
                z_b=self.prior.z_b,
                B_z_op=self.prior.B_z_op,
                obs_pred=obs_pred,
                y=obs,
                mask=mask,
                R_op=self.obs_cov_op,
            )

        # today (optimistix)
        # z* = argmin J_3D(z), started from z_b
        solution = optx.minimise(
            cost_fn,
            self.minimiser,
            self.prior.z_b,
            adjoint=self.minimiser_adjoint,
        )
        # today (pipekit_cycle)
        # x* = ψ(z*)
        return self.latent_map.decode(solution.value)  # (Nz,) → (Nx,)

    # proposed (D17)
    def as_analysis_step(self) -> pc.AnalysisStep:
        return _LatentThreeDVarAnalysisStep(self)

from typing import Any

import einx
import equinox as eqx
import jax
import lineax as lx
import optimistix as optx
import pipekit_cycle as pc
import vardax as vdx
from jaxtyping import Array, Float

# Shapes: Nx = state size; Nz = latent size; D = observations per time;
#   K = rollout steps, so T = K + 1 times in the window


# proposed (D17)
class LatentStrongFourDVar(eqx.Module):
    """Latent strong-constraint 4DVar: minimise J_4D(z_0) over z_0."""

    # today (pipekit_cycle)
    latent_map: pc.LatentMap
    # proposed (pipekit-cycle latent.md); M_z, or EncodedForwardModel
    forward: pc.LatentForwardModel
    # today (pipekit_cycle); x-space
    obs_op: pc.ObservationOperator
    # proposed (D17)
    prior: LatentPrior
    obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    n_steps: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=10)

    # today (optimistix)
    minimiser: optx.AbstractMinimiser = optx.BFGS(...)
    # today (optimistix)
    minimiser_adjoint: optx.AbstractAdjoint = optx.ImplicitAdjoint()
    # if M_z uses diffrax
    forward_adjoint: Any = None

    # today (vardax): Batch1D
    def __call__(self, batch: vdx.Batch1D) -> Float[Array, " Nx"]:
        obs_seq = batch.input
        mask_seq = batch.mask
        # proposed (pipekit-cycle latent.md)
        # H̃ = H ∘ ψ
        lifted_obs_op = pc.LiftedObservationOperator(
            decoder=self.latent_map,
            inner=self.obs_op,
        )
        observe_seq = jax.vmap(lifted_obs_op)

        def rollout(z0: Float[Array, " Nz"]) -> Float[Array, "T Nz"]:
            def step(
                z: Float[Array, " Nz"], _: None
            ) -> tuple[Float[Array, " Nz"], Float[Array, " Nz"]]:
                # proposed (pipekit-cycle latent.md)
                # zₖ₊₁ = M_z(zₖ)
                z_next = self.forward.step(z, self.forward.dt)  # (Nz,) → (Nz,)
                return z_next, z_next

            # z₁, …, z_K
            _, trajectory = jax.lax.scan(step, z0, None, length=self.n_steps)
            # (z₀, z₁, …, z_K)
            return einx.rearrange("z, k z -> (1 + k) z", z0, trajectory)

        def cost_fn(z0: Float[Array, " Nz"], args: None) -> Float[Array, ""]:
            latent_seq = rollout(z0)  # (Nz,) → (T, Nz)
            # H(ψ(zₖ)), k = 0, …, K
            obs_pred = observe_seq(latent_seq)  # (T, Nz) → (T, D)
            # proposed (D17)
            # ½‖z₀ − z_b‖²_{B_z⁻¹}
            background_term = self.prior.cost(z0)  # → ()
            # proposed (D17)
            # ½ Σₖ ‖yₖ − H(ψ(zₖ))‖²_{R⁻¹}
            obs_term = obs_misfit_latent_seq(  # → ()
                obs_pred=obs_pred,
                y_seq=obs_seq,
                mask_seq=mask_seq,
                R_op=self.obs_cov_op,
            )
            # J_4D(z₀)
            return background_term + obs_term

        # today (optimistix)
        # z₀* = argmin J_4D(z₀), started from z_b
        solution = optx.minimise(
            cost_fn,
            self.minimiser,
            self.prior.z_b,
            adjoint=self.minimiser_adjoint,
        )
        # today (pipekit_cycle)
        # x₀* = ψ(z₀*)
        return self.latent_map.decode(solution.value)  # (Nz,) → (Nx,)

(18.6) over z₀.

import einx
import equinox as eqx
import jax
import lineax as lx
import optimistix as optx
import pipekit_cycle as pc
import vardax as vdx
from jaxtyping import Array, Float

# Shapes: Nx = state size; Nz = latent size; D = observations per time;
#   K = rollout steps, so T = K + 1 times in the window


# proposed (D17)
class LatentHybridFourDVar(eqx.Module):
    """Hybrid latent 4DVar: physics forecast in x, control in z."""

    # today (pipekit_cycle)
    latent_map: pc.LatentMap
    # today (pipekit_cycle); M_x (physics)
    forward: pc.ForwardModel
    # today (pipekit_cycle)
    obs_op: pc.ObservationOperator
    # proposed (D17)
    prior: LatentPrior
    obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    n_steps: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=10)
    # today (optimistix)
    minimiser: optx.AbstractMinimiser = optx.BFGS(...)
    # today (optimistix)
    minimiser_adjoint: optx.AbstractAdjoint = optx.ImplicitAdjoint()

    # today (vardax): Batch1D
    def __call__(self, batch: vdx.Batch1D) -> Float[Array, " Nx"]:
        obs_seq = batch.input
        mask_seq = batch.mask
        observe_seq = jax.vmap(self.obs_op)

        def rollout_x(x0: Float[Array, " Nx"]) -> Float[Array, "T Nx"]:
            def step(
                x: Float[Array, " Nx"], _: None
            ) -> tuple[Float[Array, " Nx"], Float[Array, " Nx"]]:
                # today (pipekit_cycle)
                # xₖ₊₁ = M_x(xₖ)
                x_next = self.forward.step(x, self.forward.dt)  # (Nx,) → (Nx,)
                return x_next, x_next

            # x₁, …, x_K
            _, trajectory = jax.lax.scan(step, x0, None, length=self.n_steps)
            # (x₀, x₁, …, x_K)
            return einx.rearrange("x, k x -> (1 + k) x", x0, trajectory)

        def cost_fn(z0: Float[Array, " Nz"], args: None) -> Float[Array, ""]:
            # today (pipekit_cycle)
            # x₀ = ψ(z₀)
            x0 = self.latent_map.decode(z0)  # (Nz,) → (Nx,)
            # x-space rollout
            state_seq = rollout_x(x0)  # (Nx,) → (T, Nx)
            # H(xₖ), k = 0, …, K
            obs_pred = observe_seq(state_seq)  # (T, Nx) → (T, D)
            # Decoder Jacobian appears only at x0 = ψ(z_0); the rest
            # of the chain is the x-space adjoint (see §18.4.3).
            # proposed (D17)
            # ½‖z₀ − z_b‖²_{B_z⁻¹}
            background_term = self.prior.cost(z0)  # → ()
            # proposed (D17)
            # ½ Σₖ ‖yₖ − H(xₖ)‖²_{R⁻¹}
            obs_term = obs_misfit_latent_seq(  # → ()
                obs_pred=obs_pred,
                y_seq=obs_seq,
                mask_seq=mask_seq,
                R_op=self.obs_cov_op,
            )
            # J_H(z₀)
            return background_term + obs_term

        # today (optimistix)
        # z₀* = argmin J_H(z₀), started from z_b
        solution = optx.minimise(
            cost_fn,
            self.minimiser,
            self.prior.z_b,
            adjoint=self.minimiser_adjoint,
        )
        # today (pipekit_cycle)
        # x₀* = ψ(z₀*)
        analysis_x0 = self.latent_map.decode(solution.value)  # (Nz,) → (Nx,)
        analysis_seq = rollout_x(analysis_x0)  # (Nx,) → (T, Nx)
        # x₀*
        return analysis_seq[0]  # (T, Nx) → (Nx,)

The existing LaplaceCovariance lives in vardax/_src/posterior/. A
new sibling computes Laplace at the optimum in \mathcal{Z} and
returns either the z-space covariance or its pushed-forward image
via \psi:

import equinox as eqx
import jax
import lineax as lx
import vardax as vdx
from jaxtyping import Array, Float

# Shapes: Nx = state size; Nz = latent size


# proposed (D17)
class LatentLaplaceCovariance(eqx.Module):
    """Laplace approximation at z*.

    cov_z = (∇^2 J(z*))^{-1}.
    cov_x = ψ'(z*) · cov_z · ψ'(z*)^T  (when ``project=True``).
    """

    project: bool = False

    # today (vardax): Batch1D
    def __call__(
        self,
        model: LatentStrongFourDVar,
        z_star: Float[Array, " Nz"],
        batch: vdx.Batch1D,
    ) -> "_LatentPosterior | _XPosterior":
        def cost_at(z: Float[Array, " Nz"]) -> Float[Array, ""]:
            # proposed (D17)
            # J(z)
            return _cost(model, z, batch)

        # 𝐇_z(z*) = ∇²J(z*)
        hessian_matrix = jax.hessian(cost_at)(z_star)  # (Nz,) → (Nz, Nz)
        hessian = lx.MatrixLinearOperator(  # (Nz, Nz) PSD op
            hessian_matrix, lx.positive_semidefinite_tag
        )

        def solve_hessian(v: Float[Array, " Nz"]) -> Float[Array, " Nz"]:
            # 𝐇_z⁻¹ v, by a solve (the original sketch used jnp.linalg.pinv)
            return lx.linear_solve(hessian, v).value

        # cov_z = 𝐇_z(z*)⁻¹
        cov_z = lx.FunctionLinearOperator(  # (Nz, Nz) PSD op
            solve_hessian, jax.eval_shape(lambda: z_star)
        )
        if not self.project:
            # proposed (D17)
            return _LatentPosterior(
                mean_z=z_star, cov_z=cov_z, decoder=model.latent_map
            )
        # today (pipekit_cycle)
        # ψ′(z*) = ∂ψ/∂z at z*
        decoder_jacobian = lx.JacobianLinearOperator(  # (Nx, Nz) op
            lambda z, args: model.latent_map.decode(z), z_star
        )
        # cov_x = ψ′(z*) cov_z ψ′(z*)ᵀ
        cov_x = decoder_jacobian @ cov_z @ decoder_jacobian.transpose()  # (Nx, Nx) op
        # today (pipekit_cycle)
        # x* = ψ(z*)
        x_star = model.latent_map.decode(z_star)  # (Nz,) → (Nx,)
        # proposed (D17)
        return _XPosterior(mean=x_star, cov=cov_x)

import jax
import lineax as lx
import pipekit_cycle as pc
import vardax as vdx

# Shapes: Nx = 40 Lorenz-96 cells; Nz = 8 latent dims; D = 40 observations

# 1.  Pretrained AE on L96 trajectories.
# today* (vardax); satisfies pc.LatentMap today, on (B, T, Nx) arrays
# z = φ(x), x = ψ(z)
ae = vdx.BilinAEPrior1D(state_dim=40, latent_dim=8, key=...)

# 2.  Either learn a latent M_z, or wrap the physics one.
# proposed (pipekit-cycle latent.md)
# M_z = φ ∘ M_x ∘ ψ
latent_forward = pc.EncodedForwardModel(latent_map=ae, inner=l96_diffrax_model)

# 3.  Background error covariance in z (Matérn with short scale).
# proposed (gaussx); gaussx 0.0.18 has no gaussx.matern
kernel = gaussx.matern.MaternKernel(nu=1.5, length_scale=0.5)
# proposed (gaussx)
# B_z = [k(zᵢ, zⱼ)]ᵢⱼ

# proposed (D17)
# J_prior(z₀) = ½‖z₀ − z_b‖²_{B_z⁻¹}

# 4.  Latent strong-4DVar model.
# today (vardax)
# H(x) = m ⊙ x
obs_op = vdx.MaskedIdentity()  # (Nx,) → (D,)
# today* (lineax); IdentityLinearOperator takes a structure, not a size
obs_identity = lx.IdentityLinearOperator(40)
# R = σ² I
obs_cov = obs_identity * sigma_obs**2  # → (D, D) PSD op
# proposed (D17)
# z₀* = argmin J_4D(z₀)
model = vdx.LatentStrongFourDVar(
    latent_map=ae,
    forward=latent_forward,
    obs_op=obs_op,
    prior=prior,
    obs_cov_op=obs_cov,
    n_steps=20,
)

# 5.  Drive it through pipekit-cycle.
# proposed (D17)
analysis_step = model.as_analysis_step()
# proposed (pipekit-cycle latent.md)
cycle = pc.LatentDACycle(
    forward_model=latent_forward,
    latent_map=ae,
    obs_op=obs_op,
    analysis_step=analysis_step,
    obs_source=satellite_iter,
    forecast_space="z",
    update_space="z",
    re_encode_every=10**9,
    n_steps=24,
)

# today* (vardax); encode expects (B, T, Nx)
# z₀ = φ(x₀)
initial_latent = ae.encode(x0)  # (Nx,) → (Nz,)
# proposed (pipekit-cycle latent.md)
cycle_state = pc.LatentDAState(
    t=0.0, cycle_count=0, obs_err_cov=obs_cov, latent_state=initial_latent
)
# proposed (pipekit-cycle latent.md)
analyses, _ = cycle(x0, cycle_state)

records.content:
(Filed in decisions.md; summarised here for completeness.)

Latent DA is not a configuration of StrongFourDVar / ThreeDVar,
nor a wrapper around FourDVarNet. It is its own family of three
peer classes — LatentThreeDVar, LatentStrongFourDVar,
LatentHybridFourDVar — coexisting with the seven peers established
in D14.

Rationale: the control vector (z vs x), the cost dimensionality,
the Hessian object, and the posterior covariance all live in
different spaces. Burying that under a space: Literal["x", "z"]
flag would obscure the structural difference exactly the way
mode: Literal["strong", "weak"] obscured strong vs weak 4DVar in
the pre-v0.4 design.

The peer family pattern from D14 already supports the addition;
nothing in v0.4 changes.

LatentThreeDVar, LatentStrongFourDVar, LatentHybridFourDVar
importable from vardax; each implements .as_analysis_step() and
passes isinstance(., pipekit_cycle.AnalysisStep).

Existing BilinAEPrior*, MLPAEPrior*, ConvAEPrior* satisfy
pipekit_cycle.LatentMap (runtime-checkable test).

identity_latent_map(N) smoke test: latent methods reduce to their
x-space siblings within 1\mathrm{e}{-5} on Lorenz-96 with N_x =
N_z = 40.

Lorenz-96 end-to-end notebook with a real N_z = 8 AE; reports
cost-per-cycle and analysis RMSE vs. the x-space baseline.

Math reference chapter 18 lands together with the code; references
the same notation as chapters 5–8.

No regression in existing FourDVarNet* tests; the prior protocol
changes are additive only.

Latent WeakFourDVar — the model-error control vector is harder to
parameterise in \mathcal{Z}; we revisit once the strong-constraint
version is in users’ hands.

Latent AmortizedPosterior — the existing amortised posterior
already operates in a learned context space; the relationship to
LatentMap is closer to identification than addition. We will
refactor in v0.6 once LatentMap adoption is settled.

Variational autoencoders. LatentMap currently expects a
deterministic encoder; VAE support requires a sample_encode
protocol method which we defer to v0.2 of the pipekit-cycle latent
module.

Posterior in x via full pushforward. Computing
\mathrm{cov}_x = \psi'\,\mathrm{cov}_z\,{\psi'}^\top exactly is
O(N_x^2); we ship the low-rank representation by default and
expose .densify() only for small problems.

Peyron, M. et al. (2021). Latent space data assimilation by using
deep learning. QJRMS.

Cheng, S. et al. (2023). Generalised latent assimilation in
heterogeneous reduced spaces with machine learning surrogates.
J. Sci. Comput.

Fablet, R. et al. (2021). Learning variational data assimilation
models and solvers (4DVarNet). JAMES.

Bolte, J. et al. (2023). One-step differentiation of iterative
algorithms. NeurIPS.

import diffrax as dfx
import equinox as eqx
import pipekit_cycle as pc
from jaxtyping import Array, Float

# Shapes: N = state size


# today* (vardax); ships wrapping an ODE right-hand side as
# DynamicalPrior(model, params, solver, stepsize, adjoint), and
# .as_forward_model(dt) adapts it to pc.ForwardModel (D18)
class DynamicalPrior(eqx.Module):
    # today (pipekit_cycle)
    forward: pc.ForwardModel
    n_steps: int = eqx.field(static=True)
    # today (diffrax)
    forward_adjoint: dfx.AbstractAdjoint = dfx.RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint()

    def __call__(self, x: Float[Array, " N"]) -> Float[Array, " N"]:
        for _ in range(self.n_steps):
            # today (pipekit_cycle)
            # x ← M(x), over one step of length dt
            x = self.forward.step(x, self.forward.dt)  # (N,) → (N,)
        return x

import diffrax as dfx
import equinox as eqx
import lineax as lx
import optimistix as optx
import pipekit_cycle as pc
from jaxtyping import Array, Float

# Shapes: N = state size; D = observations per time; T = times in the window
# proposed (D8): Batch, the union of the vardax batch types


# today* (vardax); vardax ships forward_adjoint default None and minimiser
# default None (resolved to optx.BFGS(rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-6))
class StrongFourDVar(eqx.Module):
    # today (pipekit_cycle)
    forward: pc.ForwardModel
    # today (pipekit_cycle)
    obs_op: pc.ObservationOperator
    # x_b
    prior_mean: Float[Array, " N"]
    # B
    prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    # R
    obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    minimiser: optx.AbstractMinimiser
    # today (optimistix)
    minimiser_adjoint: optx.AbstractAdjoint = optx.ImplicitAdjoint()
    # today (diffrax)
    forward_adjoint: dfx.AbstractAdjoint = dfx.RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint()

    # x₀* = argmin J(x₀)
    def __call__(self, batch: Batch) -> Float[Array, " N"]:
        """Training / analysis interface."""
        ...

    # today (vardax)
    def as_analysis_step(self) -> pc.AnalysisStep:
        """Operational interface matching pipekit_cycle.AnalysisStep."""
        return _StrongFourDVarAnalysisStep(self)


# today* (vardax); ships as an eqx.Module
class _StrongFourDVarAnalysisStep:
    def __init__(self, model: StrongFourDVar) -> None:
        self.model = model

    def __call__(
        self,
        forecast: Float[Array, " N"],
        obs: Float[Array, "T D"],
        *,
        obs_op: pc.ObservationOperator,
        obs_err_cov: lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    ) -> Float[Array, " N"]:
        # proposed (D8)
        batch = build_batch_from_pipekit_args(forecast, obs, obs_op, obs_err_cov)
        # today* (vardax)
        # x₀* = argmin J(x₀)

records.content:
vardax operators are eqx.Module, not pipekit.Operator. To put them
in a Sequential pipeline, wrap them with pipekit.Lambda (or
JaxModelOp for persisted heads):

import pipekit as pk
import vardax as vdx

# today (pipekit); georeader_step and catalog_write_step are user operators
pipeline = pk.Sequential(
    [
        # IO
        georeader_step,
        # today (pipekit); build_batch is user
        pk.Lambda(lambda data: build_batch(data)),
        # today (pipekit)
        # x* = argmin J(x)
        pk.Lambda(lambda batch: model(batch)),
        # today (pipekit)
        # P* at x*
        pk.Lambda(posterior_adapter),
        # proposed (D10); GaussianMarkLikelihood ships without from_posterior
        pk.Lambda(vdx.GaussianMarkLikelihood.from_posterior),
        catalog_write_step,
    ]
)

(13.1) and its export in one Sequential pipeline.

Cycle orchestration — DACycle, SmootherCycle,
EnsembleDACycle, WindowedCycle come from pipekit-cycle. Vardax
does not reimplement them.

Stateful operator base class — StatefulOperator + CarryState
come from pipekit.

Loss / Callback / MetricWriter protocols — come from
pipekit-train. Vardax train_step plugs in via pipekit_train.Loss
adapters.

ModelRegistry / ExperimentTracker — come from pipekit-experiment.

After the equinox migration (Epic 0), pipekit and pipekit-cycle
become required deps. They have zero third-party dependencies
themselves, so the cost is minimal. The current v0.1.x package
(previously published as fourdvarjax) does not yet declare them in
pyproject.toml; the dependency policy described here is a v0.4
design target.

pipekit-jax, pipekit-experiment, pipekit-train are planned as
optional extras (vardax[persist], vardax[train]).

The test module below is part of the planned Epic 1 conformance suite
— not yet present in the v0.1.6 codebase.

Per Decision D10, every vardax analysis emits a Posterior container —
not just a point estimate. The posterior carries enough information to feed
downstream population models (Tier V TMTPP, hierarchical Bayesian
inversions) without re-running the inner inference.

Two of the seven Layer 2 classes have closed-form fast paths that emit
the posterior as part of the analysis call:

OptimalInterpolation — closed-form P^* = (B^{-1} + H^\top R^{-1} H)^{-1}
is returned directly by .posterior(batch).

IncrementalFourDVar — the Gauss-Newton Hessian assembled during
the last outer iteration is reused for P^*.

For the other five (ThreeDVar, StrongFourDVar, WeakFourDVar,
FourDVarNet, AmortizedPosterior), pair the analysis with an
explicit PosteriorAdapter.

import equinox as eqx
import lineax as lx
from jaxtyping import Array, Float

# Shapes: N = state size; M = ensemble members or flow samples;
#   *window = optional leading batch of windows


# today* (vardax)
class Posterior(eqx.Module):
    # x*, the MAP or posterior mean
    mean: Float[Array, "*window N"]
    # P*, a gaussx / lineax operator; None for sampling-only heads
    cov: lx.AbstractLinearOperator | None
    # x⁽ᵐ⁾, m = 1, …, M, for ensemble and flow heads
    samples: Float[Array, "*window M N"] | None
    # forward_model_id, n_iter, J_star, …
    provenance: dict

Program 1:Declares the Posterior container that every analysis returns, carrying the mean x* and covariance P* of 

(4.3) (Decision D10).

Conventions:

mean — always populated.

cov — None for amortized samples / score-based heads. Otherwise an
AbstractLinearOperator supporting mat-vec (not necessarily
materialised).

samples — None for Laplace / GN-Hessian (Gaussian-only). Populated
for ensemble / flow heads.

provenance — dict with at minimum {forward_model_id, obs_ops_used, n_iter, J_star, converged, gaussx_op_hash, model_hash}.

At the MAP x^*:P^* = \big(H'^\top R^{-1} H' + B^{-1}\big)^{-1}

where H' = \partial H / \partial x at x^*. Returned as an
AbstractLinearOperator so mat-vec via lineax.CG is cheap; full
materialisation only on request.

When to use. Gaussian likelihood, single mode, MAP near posterior mean
(confirmed by SBC). Default for IncrementalFourDVar.

Cost. One Hessian-vector product family per query. Posterior samples by
x^* + (H'^\top R^{-1} H' + B^{-1})^{-1/2} \xi where \xi \sim \mathcal{N}(0,I) —
requires square-root which may be expensive for unstructured B.

from jaxtyping import Array, Float

# Shapes: N = state size
# today (pipekit_cycle): AnalysisStep
# today (vardax): Posterior
# proposed (D10): Batch, the union of the vardax batch types


# today* (vardax)
class LaplaceCovariance(eqx.Module):
    # P* = (H′ᵀ R⁻¹ H′ + B⁻¹)⁻¹, with H′ = ∂H/∂x at x*
    def __call__(
        self,
        analysis: Float[Array, " N"],
        model: AnalysisStep,
        batch: Batch,
    ) -> Posterior: ...

(13.1) at the MAP as a lazy operator.

Krylov / Lanczos inversion of J''(x^*) via lineax.CG. For incremental
4DVar this is the natural posterior — the inner Hessian is already assembled
during the last outer iteration.

When to use. Operational incremental 4DVar (IncrementalFourDVar). The
Hessian operator from the last GN outer iteration is reused.

Cost. n_krylov mat-vec products. Materialise only the diagonal /
required marginals.

Per-event posteriors feed Tier V (TMTPP, hierarchical Bayesian) via a
mark-likelihood serialisation:

from typing import Any

import equinox as eqx

# Shapes: N = state size; M = ensemble members or flow samples
# today (vardax): Posterior


# today* (vardax)
# ships to_dict with keys mean, cov_diag, samples, provenance, event_metadata
class GaussianMarkLikelihood(eqx.Module):
    """Posterior → mark-likelihood for population models (Tier V, Decision D10)."""

    posterior: Posterior
    # event_id, time, location, instruments_used, …
    event_metadata: dict

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        metadata = self.event_metadata
        samples = self.posterior.samples
        # x* as nested lists
        mean = self.posterior.mean.tolist()  # (N,) → list
        # proposed (D10)
        # P* as a diagonal, Cholesky or low-rank record
        cov = self._serialise_cov()  # (N, N) op → dict
        # x⁽ᵐ⁾ as nested lists, or None
        sample_list = None if samples is None else samples.tolist()  # (M, N) → list
        return {
            "event_id": metadata["event_id"],
            "time": metadata["time"],
            "geometry": metadata["geometry"],
            "mean": mean,
            "cov": cov,
            "samples": sample_list,
            "provenance": self.posterior.provenance,
        }

    # proposed (D10)
    def _serialise_cov(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Serialise gaussx AbstractLinearOperator to JSON-compatible form."""
        ...

Program 5:Serialises a Posterior, the Gaussian of 

(4.3), into a JSON mark-likelihood for Tier V population models (Decision D10).

The serialised form is consumed by population models without
re-instantiating the vardax inference — Tier V improvements automatically
absorb upgrades to Tier I-IV forwards.

Six-step cycle requires:

Posterior agreement. Step 4 (emulator MAP) within 1\sigma_\text{post}
of Step 2 (physics MAP). Failed when CV(amortized) / CV(physics) > 2 or
when |mean_amortized - mean_physics| / σ_physics > 1.

Adjoint calibration. \|\partial H_\text{em} / \partial x - \partial H_\text{phys} / \partial x\|_\text{op} < 5\%
measured by random-vector probing.

Simulation-based calibration (SBC). Rank histograms uniform across
parameters, stratified by met regime. Failed when the χ² test of
uniformity rejects at p < 0.01.

These gates run on a held-out validation set in CI:

# tests/test_six_step_validation.py
import equinox as eqx
import vardax as vdx
from jaxtyping import Array, Float

# Shapes: N = state size; D = observations per window; V = held-out states


def test_posterior_agreement(
    physics_model: eqx.Module,
    emulator_model: eqx.Module,
    val_batches: list[vdx.Batch1D],
) -> None:
    # today (vardax)
    laplace = vdx.LaplaceCovariance()
    for batch in val_batches:
        # today* (vardax)
        # x*_phys = argmin J_phys(x)
        physics_analysis = physics_model(batch)  # → (N,)
        # today* (vardax)
        # x*_em = argmin J_em(x)
        emulator_analysis = emulator_model(batch)  # → (N,)
        # today (vardax)
        # P*_phys = (H′ᵀ R⁻¹ H′ + B⁻¹)⁻¹ at x*_phys
        physics_posterior = laplace(physics_analysis, physics_model, batch)
        # today (vardax)
        # P*_em at x*_em
        emulator_posterior = laplace(emulator_analysis, emulator_model, batch)
        # today (vardax)
        # |x*_em − x*_phys| / σ_post,phys ≤ 1
        vdx.assert_posterior_agreement(
            emulator_posterior, physics_posterior, tolerance_sigma=1.0
        )


def test_adjoint_calibration(
    physics_obs_op: vdx.ObservationOperator,
    emulator_obs_op: vdx.ObservationOperator,
    val_states: Float[Array, "V N"],
) -> None:
    for state in val_states:
        # today (vardax)
        # H′_phys = ∂H_phys/∂x at x
        physics_tangent = physics_obs_op.linearize(state)  # (N,) → (D, N) op
        # today (vardax)
        # H′_em = ∂H_em/∂x at x
        emulator_tangent = emulator_obs_op.linearize(state)  # (N,) → (D, N) op
        # proposed (D12); vdx.assert_adjoint_calibrated ships the probing gate
        # ‖H′_em − H′_phys‖_op, by 20 random-vector probes
        op_norm = estimate_operator_norm_diff(  # → ()
            physics_tangent, emulator_tangent, n_probe=20
        )
        assert op_norm < 0.05

This schema is the contract between the inference layer (vardax) and the
audit layer (catalog / database). Don’t break it lightly.

vardax is the data assimilation inference layer for JAX. It provides
the seven classical and modern analysis methods that turn observations
into state estimates:

OptimalInterpolation — BLUE / OI, the closed-form linear-Gaussian
analysis. The right tool when H is linear and B, R are Gaussian.

ThreeDVar — 3D variational analysis. Nonlinear observation
operator, snapshot in time.

StrongFourDVar — strong-constraint 4DVar. Control variable is
the initial state x_0; dynamics M_t are treated as exact.

WeakFourDVar — weak-constraint 4DVar. Augmented control vector
(x_0, \eta_1, \ldots, \eta_T) admits model error.

IncrementalFourDVar — the operational fast path of strong-constraint
4DVar. Gauss-Newton outer iterations on the full nonlinear cost, CG
inner iterations on the linearised quadratic subproblem, control-variable
transform for preconditioning.

FourDVarNet — the learned variant of 4DVar. Prior \varphi_\theta
replaces the Gaussian B; the inner solver becomes a learned gradient
modulator \Phi_\phi.

AmortizedPosterior — the direct head q_\phi(x \mid y). Real-time
inference via conditional flow, score-based diffusion, or regression.

All seven are siblings, not parent–child relationships. They satisfy the
same pipekit_cycle.AnalysisStep protocol and compose with the same
observation operators, forward models, priors, and posterior adapters.
The DA hierarchy is horizontal; you pick the method that matches the
regime, not a family.

Every analysis method in vardax is a special case ofx^* = \underset{x,\,\boldsymbol{\eta}}{\arg\min}\;
  \underbrace{\tfrac{1}{2}\|x - x_b\|^2_{B^{-1}}}_{\text{background term}}
  + \underbrace{\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{t=0}^{T} \|y_t - H_t(M_t(x; \boldsymbol{\eta}))\|^2_{R_t^{-1}}}_{\text{observation term}}
  \;[\,+\;\underbrace{\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{t=1}^{T} \|\eta_t\|^2_{Q_t^{-1}}}_{\text{model-error term}}\,].
